newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa body increases 96/97 wheat crop estimate.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa body increases 96/97 wheat crop estimate.

text.p: South Africa's National Crop Estimates Committee said on Monday it had increased its estimate of the 1996/97 wheat crop to 2.753 million tonnes from a forecast 2.593 million tonnes in December.
The committee said the 160,000 tonne increase on its December 20 forecast was largely due to better growing prospects in the Western Cape and Free State provinces.
"There was a major increase in the Western Cape where the yield is much better than expected. This is also the case in the eastern Free State," a spokesman told Reuters.
He said the crop estimate for barley was unchanged at 176,000 tonnes where it was pegged in December.
Wheat industry sources said earlier this month South Africa may not need to import any wheat for breadmaking -- the first time in eight years this has occurred -- following a bumper crop this season.
Commercial milling needs are seen at around 2.462 million tonnes, creating the possibility that the country may be able to export a small surplus, the National Chamber of Milling told Reuters.
Other types of wheat, including durum, a hard grain used for making pasta, and soft biscuit-making wheat would, however need to be imported, the chamber said.
